summary: Jackson County lookout tower on Battle Mountain, built in stages from 1933 to 1936, closed in 1957, manned again in 1963, and gone by 1965-1970s depending on source.

facts.design: Tree crow's nest and tent or camp (1933), then a pole tower and log cabin (1935), then a 40-to-41-foot tower with an L-4 cab (1936)
facts.status_note: Register says removed and destroyed in 1965; Forest Lookouts says destroyed in 1967; Firelookout says gone in the 1970s. No source describes the site today.

corrections.proposed: 1933 first structure was a crow's nest and tent; the tower dates to 1935-1936
corrections.why: The register's own description gives 1933 for a crow's nest and tent, not a tower. Forest Lookouts quotes a late-October 1935 item reporting the new tower completed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says destroyed 1965; Forest Lookouts logs destroyed 1967; Firelookout says abandoned, gone 1970s. The story gives all three.

Register and Firelookout say a 40-to-41-foot tower in 1936; Forest Lookouts quotes a 1935 completion and a 1936 letter saying 50 feet. The story keeps both and the brief's 12.2 m height matches the 40-to-41-foot figure.

Register says Oregon Department of Forestry; Firelookout says Southwest Oregon FPA; Forest Lookouts uses Southwest Oregon Fire Patrol; the 1943 NGS data sheet on Forest Lookouts calls it a Forest Service lookout. Facts keep the register's agency.
Register and Firelookout say 1933; a 1918 item quoted on Forest Lookouts says a log cabin was being built on the summit in 1918. Both appear in the story.

notes_for_editor: The brief record shows 1933 built and 1965 removed from the register's fields. The register's description and the other two sources disagree on the tower dates and fate. Staffing is recorded as last documented in the 1963 season; the earlier 'unstaffed as of 1967' was the destruction date and had no staffing source, so it was replaced. A 1970 placeholder event was dropped; the 1970s comes from Firelookout's status note only. The NGS data sheet linked from Forest Lookouts was read: a 1943 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description that calls the lookout a Forest Service lookout and says the station was not marked and not visited by that party. It describes 1943, not today, so the 'no source describes the site today' note stands. One WebSearch was used and yielded only unrelated 2024 fire results, so it was not cited.
